business_patterns.top_pattern: Authorization code distribution changes are a gating issue before action
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Medicaid inpatient authorization coding and mapping in CA, AR, and IN
key_driver_codes: Major Small and Large Bowel Procedures with CC
Esophagitis, Gastroenteritis and Miscellaneous Digestive Disorders without MCC
Cirrhosis and Alcoholic Hepatitis with CC
business_patterns.pattern_details: A large share of the increase is tied to authorization code distribution changes rather than a clean utilization or reimbursement signal. CA is the largest exposure, with the same issue also appearing in AR and IN. This should be treated as a front-end validation problem before any medical management or provider action is taken.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: If the authorization-to-claim mapping is unstable, follow-on actions on utilization, reimbursement, or provider performance could target the wrong root cause.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Have UM operations and data quality validate the authorization code mapping in CA, AR, and IN, then reissue a corrected spend view before launching provider or policy interventions.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The findings are explicitly flagged as authorization or mapping shifts that require validation before business action.
evidence_summary: CA accounts for +$6.2M of the issue across four inpatient DRGs, led by bowel procedures at +$2.3M and digestive disorders at +$2.2M.
AR adds +$1.4M from the same authorization code distribution issue.
IN adds +$1.2M, concentrated in Cirrhosis and Alcoholic Hepatitis with CC.
No admission or paid-per-admit metrics support a clean utilization or unit-cost interpretation because this is a coding or mapping validation pattern.

business_patterns.top_pattern: DC authorized inpatient spend is distorted by facility classification and site-of-care mix
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: DC Medicaid authorized inpatient facility classification and site-of-care mix
business_patterns.pattern_details: DC has a concentrated increase in authorized inpatient spend tied to facility buckets labeled Not Mapped and OTHER. The pattern is present across TANF Standard and ABD Non Dual, with both more admissions and higher paid per admission. This looks like a mix of real site-of-care pressure and facility classification drift, so classification cleanup and business action need to run together.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Without fixing facility attribution, the plan cannot reliably separate true provider mix changes from data classification noise in one of the largest state-level increases.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Correct DC facility mapping for authorized inpatient claims first, then run a focused UM and reimbursement review on the TANF Standard and ABD Non Dual admissions driving the remaining increase.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Facility values of Not Mapped and OTHER mean the plan cannot cleanly determine whether the increase reflects true site-of-care movement, provider mix, or mapping error.
evidence_summary: DC TANF Standard with facility Not Mapped drove +$4.5M from 92 more admissions and about +$31.2K paid per admit.
DC TANF Standard with facility OTHER added +$1.3M with 57 more admissions and about +$1.9K paid per admit.
DC ABD Non Dual with facility Not Mapped added +$0.6M with 16 more admissions and about +$37.7K paid per admit.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA acute hospital admissions are rising with higher paid per admit in authorized Medicaid products
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA Medicaid acute hospital authorized admissions
key_driver_codes: Esophagitis, Gastroenteritis and Miscellaneous Digestive Disorders without MCC
Major Small and Large Bowel Procedures with CC
business_patterns.pattern_details: CA shows the largest clean operational growth pattern after validation issues are set aside. Authorized acute hospital spend is rising in TANF Standard and ABD Non Dual because admissions are up and paid per admit is also increasing. The pressure is concentrated in digestive, bowel, liver, obesity, and nerve disorder admissions rather than a broad all-category trend.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is actionable spend growth with both utilization and unit-cost pressure, so UM, reimbursement, and provider outreach can all affect the outcome.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run a CA acute-hospital action plan for TANF Standard and ABD Non Dual that pairs admission management with claim-level review of the highest-cost DRGs and reimbursement terms.
evidence_summary: CA TANF Standard acute hospital drove +$5.6M across digestive, bowel, cirrhosis, obesity, and nerve disorder DRGs.
The largest CA driver was digestive disorders at +$2.0M with 248 more admissions and about +$3.1K higher paid per admit.
CA bowel procedures added +$1.7M with 60 more admissions and about +$14.2K higher paid per admit.
CA ABD Non Dual acute hospital added +$0.6M with 74 more admissions and about +$3.3K higher paid per admit.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA inpatient case mix is shifting toward digestive, liver, obesity, and neuropathy admissions
business_patterns.pattern_details: CA also has a distinct clinical story separate from the operational acute-hospital mix. Growth is concentrated in recurring digestive, liver, obesity, and neuropathy diagnoses, with some emerging small-volume cases layered on top. Much of the increase appears volume-led, but some diagnoses also show higher intensity or higher paid per admit.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This pattern points to targeted clinical and UM interventions in specific diagnoses rather than a generic inpatient trend.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Prioritize CA clinical review pathways for cirrhosis, obesity surgery, neuropathy, and GI admissions, and pair them with utilization management rules for repeatable admission drivers.
evidence_summary: CA clinical case-mix groups total +$5.3M across recurring and emerging diagnoses.
Alcoholic cirrhosis with ascites added +$0.8M with 66 more admissions even as paid per admit fell slightly.
Metabolic syndrome within obesity procedures added +$0.8M with 35 more admissions.
Noninfective gastroenteritis and colitis added +$0.4M with 56 more admissions and about +$1.0K paid per admit.

business_patterns.top_pattern: NC spend is highly concentrated at DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: NC Medicaid admissions concentrated at DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC
key_driver_codes: Heart Transplant or Implant of Heart Assist System with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: NC growth is concentrated in one provider, DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC, across both operational and clinical signals. The pattern combines higher authorized admission volume in Not Mapped facility claims with a small number of very high-cost transplant-related cases. This is a concentrated provider economics story, but mapping issues need to be resolved so the true facility and payment picture is clear.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A single-provider concentration of this size can move results quickly, but actions will differ depending on whether the increase is driven by legitimate case severity, facility attribution, or reimbursement terms.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Open a joint network, UM, and data-quality review with DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC to separate transplant outliers from mapped inpatient growth and confirm the correct facility attribution on Not Mapped claims.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Not Mapped facility values and a small not-mapped clinical outlier mean provider concentration should be confirmed before taking reimbursement or utilization action.
evidence_summary: DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC heart transplant and assist-system cases added +$1.6M from 3 admissions, including one case at +$1.0M.
DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC TANF Standard Not Mapped utilization added +$1.6M from 20 more admissions despite lower paid per admit, showing volume-led growth.
DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC ABD Non Dual Not Mapped added +$0.8M with 9 more admissions and about +$89.3K paid per admit.
An additional not-mapped DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC clinical case added +$0.2M, reinforcing the attribution issue.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Rare catastrophic inpatient cases are creating discrete high-cost spikes
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Rare catastrophic inpatient episodes across UNATTRIBUTED, AR, DC, FL, NC, OH, and VA
key_driver_codes: Tracheostomy with Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours or Principal Diagnosis Except Face, Mouth and Neck without Major O.R. Procedures
Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with MCC
Extensive Burns or Full Thickness Burns with Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours with Skin Graft
ECMO or Tracheostomy with Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours or Principal Diagnosis Except Face, Mouth and Neck with Major O.R. Procedures
business_patterns.pattern_details: Several states show isolated catastrophic inpatient episodes rather than a recurring utilization trend. These include tracheostomy and prolonged ventilation, craniotomy, burns, ECMO-level care, transplant, trauma, and other severe cases with very high paid amounts on very small numbers of admissions. The right response is claim-level and clinical validation, not broad policy changes.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A handful of catastrophic cases can materially move spend, but they require one-case-at-a-time review instead of broad network or utilization actions.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Route these cases to clinical and payment integrity review to confirm severity, coding, contract terms, and outlier payment treatment before changing medical policy or provider strategy.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Most of the increase is driven by one-off or very small-count high-cost admissions, so claim-level confirmation is needed before generalizing the pattern.
evidence_summary: A single DC tracheostomy and prolonged mechanical ventilation case added +$1.3M on 1 admission.
A DC craniotomy case added another +$0.7M on 1 admission.
AR trauma, pneumonia, and GI obstruction cases contributed about +$1.0M across 10 admissions.
Rare burn, ECMO, and transplant episodes across FL, NC, OH, and VA added about +$0.9M, led by two SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL cases totaling +$0.6M.

business_patterns.top_pattern: VA spend is concentrated at SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL across volume and unit-cost signals
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: VA Medicaid admissions concentrated at SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL
business_patterns.pattern_details: VA shows a concentrated provider story at SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL. Most of the increase comes from additional admissions in Not Mapped facility claims, while a separate acute-hospital pocket shows unit-cost pressure even as admissions decline. This is a focused provider economics and attribution pattern rather than a broad VA-wide inpatient trend.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A concentrated provider pattern can often be addressed faster through direct contract, authorization, and data-quality work than through broad market interventions.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Perform a provider-specific review with SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL to fix facility attribution on Not Mapped claims and assess whether the acute-hospital paid-per-admit increase needs reimbursement or UM intervention.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The largest VA drivers sit in Not Mapped facility claims, so facility attribution needs to be corrected to distinguish real provider mix changes from mapping error.
evidence_summary: VA ABD Non Dual Not Mapped volume added +$0.4M at SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL.
VA TANF Standard Not Mapped volume added +$0.3M at the same provider.
VA TANF Standard acute hospital added +$0.2M from 21 more admissions even though paid per admit fell slightly.
A separate VA TANF Standard acute-hospital unit-cost increase added +$0.2M while admissions declined by 8, showing reimbursement pressure on top of volume shifts.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Smaller state and product pockets show emerging authorized inpatient pressure
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Smaller Medicaid authorized inpatient pockets across MD, MO, WV, AR, IN, NY, FL, OH, and CO
business_patterns.pattern_details: Outside the largest state and provider concentrations, there is a set of smaller authorized inpatient pockets that are individually modest but together meaningful. These pockets are spread across acute hospital, children's, acute psych, and some Not Mapped facility claims. Most are low-baseline or low-volume, so they should be managed as a targeted exception list rather than as an enterprise trend.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: These pockets are actionable if handled as targeted state-product worklists, but they are too fragmented and low-volume to justify a broad strategy.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Create a state-product exception queue for MD, MO, WV, AR, IN, NY, FL, OH, and CO, and assign each pocket to UM or network teams for targeted review of admission growth, paid-per-admit changes, and any remaining mapping gaps.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Many of these pockets are low-volume, low-baseline, or include Not Mapped facility values, so targeted review should confirm persistence before large-scale action.
evidence_summary: MD, MO, and WV TANF Standard acute hospital added +$1.1M, led by MD bowel procedures at +$0.5M and MO digestive disorders at +$0.5M.
AR LTSS Non Dual added +$0.5M in CHILDRENS and another +$0.3M across Not Mapped and ACUTE PSYCH settings.
IN Family Care acute hospital added +$0.5M across cirrhosis and nerve disorder admissions, and NY Family Care acute hospital added +$0.3M from obesity procedures.
FL, OH, and CO contain smaller ABD or Family Care pockets that are low-volume exceptions rather than a broad trend.

executive_summary.headline: The highest-impact story is a mix of authorization mapping issues, concentrated provider and facility classification shifts, and a smaller set of real inpatient case-mix and catastrophic outlier pressures.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: Two validation themes need to be resolved first: authorization code distribution changes in CA, AR, and IN, and facility attribution issues in DC, NC, and VA where Not Mapped values are driving large portions of the increase. Once those are cleaned up, the most actionable real spend drivers are CA acute-hospital growth, CA clinical case-mix expansion, and concentrated provider economics at DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC and SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL.
recommended_focus_order: Fix authorization code distribution and facility mapping validation issues first.
Address CA and DC Medicaid inpatient growth next because they are the largest operational cost levers.
Then work concentrated provider cases at DUKE UNIVERSITY HEALTH SYSTEM INC and SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL, followed by rare catastrophic outliers and smaller state-product pockets.

notes: All 34 analytical groups were assigned to 8 business patterns.
Authorization validation and facility attribution issues were kept separate because they represent different gating problems.
Low-volume multi-state operational pockets were intentionally consolidated into one exception-worklist pattern to preserve the 8-pattern limit.
Rare catastrophic clinical outliers were kept separate from recurring CA clinical case-mix growth because the downstream action differs.
Segment attribution is weak for 61% of cards (51 of 84) on segment_by [service_area_state]; add those dimensions to the stage's dimension or carry-through list to attribute them at cell level.
Merged 11 immaterial segment group(s) into residual groups labelled with their literal segment values.
